summary: Michael Oppitz works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He held a post at the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin from around 1989 to 1990 and served at the University of Zurich from approximately 1991 to 2008.

Michael Puett is a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1988–1994) under committee member Anthony C. Yu, and became John L. Loeb Associate Professor of Humanities at Harvard University around 1994.

Michael Pye works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied under Maurice Wiles and Jørn Borup, later holding posts at the University of Leeds (~1974–1980) and as a professor at Lancaster University (~1995–1999).

Michael Radich is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at Harvard University (~2001–2007) and studied at Kyoto University (2009). He served as a lecturer at Victoria University of Wellington (~2007–2017) before joining Heidelberg University around 2017.
Michael S. Drummond is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at the University of Bristol and studied as a PhD candidate at Utrecht University.

Michael Schmidt specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Göttingen and served as a Mitarbeiter at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities from 1981 to 1992.
Michael Scott Carroll is a scholar of philosophy and Sinology. He earned an MPhil at the University of Hong Kong (~2004–2006), where he studied under committee member Dale S. Wright.

Michael Sheehy works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies (~2001–2007) under Steven D. Goodman. He held posts at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (~2013–2017) and the University of Virginia (~2019).

Michael Stanley-Baker works in Sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He earned an MA at Indiana University (~2003–2006) under Stephen R. Bokenkamp. His posts include MPIWG (~2012–2017), University of Pittsburgh (~2017–2018), Leipzig University, and Nanyang Technological University (~2018).
Michael Szonyi is a historian and Sinologist. He studied at Merton College from around 1989 to 1994 and took up a post at Harvard University around 2005.
Michael Torsten Much specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied as a fellow at the University of Hamburg and studied under Ernst Steinkellner from around 1978 to 1984.
Michael Viggo Fausbøll was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1838–1847) and later held a post there from around 1878 to 1902.

Michael W. Meister is a specialist in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania (until ~1971) and Harvard University (~1964–1974), and became a professor at the University of Pennsylvania around 1976.

Michael Witzel specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Paul Thieme (~1965–1971) and served as director at the Nepal Research Centre (~1972–1977), Chair of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1980–1987), and Chair of Sanskrit at Harvard University (1987–2013).

Michael Zimmermann specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg (~1993–2000) under Lambert Schmithausen and others. He held posts at Stanford University (2003–2007) and the University of Hamburg (~2007).

Michael von Brück is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Regensburg from around 1988 to 1991 and at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich from approximately 1991 to 2014.

Michaela Haas works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Bonn by 2008 under doctoral supervisor Peter Schwieger, and also studied under Konrad Klaus, Jigme Namgyal, and Rechungpa.

Michaela Mross specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She earned her PhD at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (-2014), held a fellowship at UC Berkeley (~2014–2016), and became Assistant Professor of Japanese Buddhism at Stanford University around 2017.

Michel Bréal was a linguist and Indologist who studied at École Normale Supérieure (~1852–1855) and under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp. He was a professor at Collège de France (1866–1905) and director at École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1868–1882).
Michel Clasquin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at the University of South Africa, completing his doctoral thesis by 1999, and held a post there beginning in 1990.
